title: Backend developer roadmap
summary: Follow an ordered path from first programs to a deployed API, with a milestone to check at each phase.
learningObjectives: Know the order of the phases and why
Define a checkable milestone for each phase
keyTakeaways: Milestones are things you build, not things you read
explanation:
This path assumes about **6 hours a week**. Double the hours and the durations roughly halve; halve them and they double.

What is left out on purpose: container orchestration, advanced distributed systems and deep performance tuning. They matter later, not first.

blocks.title: A realistic path

phases.label: Programming basics
phases.goal: Write small programs in one language without copying

phases.label: Web and HTTP
phases.goal: Build a simple API and call it
milestones: Create a REST API with 4 endpoints

phases.label: Databases
phases.goal: Store and query data with SQL
milestones: Write a join and an index

phases.label: Deploy and operate
phases.goal: Ship the API to a server and keep it running
milestones: Add logging and a health check

blocks.note: Durations assume about 6 hours a week; scale them to your own pace. SAMPLE DATA for testing.

nodes.question: Do you prefer a gentle, readable language?

nodes.outcome: Java: strict, common in large companies

commonMistakes: Skipping fundamentals to chase a framework
Following tutorials without building anything of your own

quiz.question: Why do databases come after the web and HTTP phase here?
options: An API needs somewhere to keep data, so you build the API first
quiz.explanation: The order follows dependency: you need an API before you know what to store.

quiz.question: What does a good milestone look like?
options: Deploy an API with a public URL
quiz.explanation: A milestone is something you can build and check.

quiz.question: You are two weeks behind. What is the best response?
options: Keep the order and extend the dates
quiz.explanation: The order is the point; adjust the pace, not the sequence.

recommendedResources.title: MDN: Server-side website programming
recommendedResources.searchQuery: MDN server-side website programming first steps

socraticChallenge.scenario: You have 3 hours a week instead of 6.
socraticChallenge.question: How would you adjust the path?
socraticChallenge.idealAnswer: Keep the same order, double the durations, and keep one build-something milestone per phase.

exercises.prompt: Write what you will build in weeks 1 to 4 at your own pace.
exercises.answer: A small command-line project with a named finish line, for example a to-do app that saves to a file by the end of week 4.

reviewCards.prompt: Why does the database phase come after building a simple API?
reviewCards.answer: Because the API shows what data you need to store.
